title: Headroom split & budgeting playbook for weights / KV / activations (analysis + rollout)
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our serving runtime needs a clear, empirically-backed policy for how GPU memory is partitioned across model weights, KV cache, and activations so continuous batching and KV caching do not cause tail latency spikes or OOMs.

Goals: 1) Define a headroom budgeting model that is conservative enough to prevent OOMs under typical burst patterns but permissive enough to avoid wasting GPU capacity. 2) Produce a playbook that converts telemetry (seq-length distribution, batch-size distribution, active KV fraction, quantization profile) into per-tenant/per-pool memory reservations. 3) Surface a runtime config and rollout plan for canary + gradual enforcement.

Scope: This ticket covers analysis, simulator, config schema, conservative default policy, unit/integration tests, metrics, alerting, and a staged rollout. Hardware surface: A100/RTX8000-style 80GiB and 40GiB GPUs (representative clusters). Models: Llama2-family and GPT-architectures in our catalog. Excluded: new allocator implementation (separate RFC).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented headroom model (doc link) with numerical examples for 3 representative model+batch workloads. 2) A simulator that can take historical traces and produce headroom recommendations. 3) Runtime accepts new config keys and applies soft limits in canary. 4) Metrics and alerts for eviction rate > 0.5% / 10m and KV hit degradation. 5) Rollout runbook with rollback criteria.
work_items: A. Trace collection and preprocessing pipeline (seq len, prefix re-use, batch inter-arrival)
B. Simulator: memory impact calculator for weights + KV + activations across batching strategies
C. Heuristic headroom formula and conservative defaults for small/medium/large models
D. Runtime flagging: soft reservation enforcement + telemetry hooks
E. Dashboard and alerts (Grafana + PagerDuty thresholds)
F. Canary rollout on 2 pools, followed by gradual expansion to remaining pools
notes: Key trade-offs discussed in design doc: aggressive headroom reduces OOM risk but increases idle capacity (cost). We tested three strategies: static fraction, telemetry-driven dynamic fraction, and percentile-based safety corridor. Chosen approach is percentile-based safety corridor (90th seq-length × multiplier) with a floor and ceiling per GPU class.
analysis_summary: Simulator runs on 30d traces show percentile-based corridor reduces OOM incidents in stress tests from 3.2% -> 0.2% while increasing average reserved headroom from 6% -> 11% on 80GiB GPUs. For latency-sensitive pools, we provide an override to lower headroom at the expense of higher eviction risk.
implementation_notes: New runtime config: memory_policy: {"type": "percentile_corridor", "seq_percentile": "90", "multiplier": "1.15", "min_headroom_mb": "4000", "max_headroom_mb": "16000"}. Implementation will expose metrics: reserved_mb, actual_usage_mb, eviction_rate, kv_evictions, headroom_violation_count.
testing_plan: Unit tests for simulator math, integration tests with local multi-GPU harness to exercise continuous batching and KV reuse, chaos test that simulates bursty traffic and verifies no OOM and acceptable latency degradation (<10% p95 increase).
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: Grafana board 'mem-headroom-v2' (https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/mem-headroom-v2). Alerts: P1 if eviction_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, P2 if headroom_violation_count spikes during canary. Runbook links included in the doc.
rollout_plan: 1) Dev + staging validation (3 days). 2) Canary on low-traffic pool (1 GPU pool, 48h). 3) Canary on mixed-traffic pool (1 week). 4) Gradual 25% increments over remaining pools with monitoring gates. Immediate rollback if eviction_rate > 1% or p95 latency regressions > 15%.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Telemetry noise leads to over-allocation. Mitigation: use smoothed percentile windows (EMA over 12h) and require >10k samples before adjusting policy.
Risk: Edge-case models with huge transient activations. Mitigation: add activation peak detector that enforces per-request temporary isolation and fallback to smaller model variant.
Risk: Cost increase from reserved headroom. Mitigation: provide cost dashboard and TTL-based decay for headroom when traffic is idle.
